mode.why: third-party product teaser of unknown origin: borrow the motion language and look only, never its shots one by one, its app UI, its logo, its copy or its photos (owner note); a voiceover package defaults to REEL

ignored.why: all English copy ('What's inside one click?', 'Drop everything in.', 'photos. videos. chaos.', 'Pick a mood.', 'dreamy. loud.', 'Every cut on the beat.', 'That was one click.', 'Your film is ready.', the tagline, 'AI VIDEO EDITOR', 'Coming soon') is third-party copy; never reused as text
the phone app screen (thumbnail grid, DREAMY/SOFT/LOUD chips, round record button) is a third-party UI design; only the dotted-outline drawing and the click-into-the-button push are borrowed
the photos and clips inside the cards (dog, people, concert, beach) are the reference's own footage and story props; our cards show subjects from the voice-over or the owner's assets
the dot-matrix wordmark 'ROLIK' and its badge are a third-party logo; our film ends on the brand's own logo outro, only the dot-assembly motion is borrowed
the audio track is third-party music; L6 builds our own sound

method: ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2 (4 sheets, 4x3, all viewed); scene detect gt(scene,0.3) found cuts at 2.25, 4.00/4.08, 6.21, 7.75-8.08, 11.79, 14.50, 15.00, 15.50, 15.75, 16.00, 16.25, 16.75, 17.46, 21.00/21.08 s; dense sheets fps=12 over 1.75-2.75 s, fps=6 over 5.75-8.25 s and 14.25-17.75 s (3 sheets, all viewed); silencedetect + volumedetect on the audio. Spans accurate to about ±0.1 s from the sheets, cut times to one frame from scene detect. Colours read by eye, not sampled.

shots.moves: a small dot and a big black disc sit on the page (0 s); a caption types in letter by letter at the left with a round dot as the cursor at its end (0.3-0.8 s); the disc splits into a few dots that drift into a 3x3 grid (0.5-1.0 s, smooth ease-out); a dotted outline draws itself around the grid as a device frame and the dots become its contents and button (1.0-1.4 s); a cursor arrives and presses the round button (ring pulse, about 1.9 s); the caption collapses into a short Morse-like string of dots and dashes; the camera pushes into the button until the black disc fills the frame, halftone dots spilling from its edge (2.0-2.2 s)

shots.transition_out: match cut through the dot: the black button grows to fill the frame and the next world starts on black (cut at 2.25 s)

shots.reusable: yes: one dot as the hero actor that splits, arranges and is framed; an outline drawn as a dotted line; typing with a dot cursor; a push-in into a dot that becomes the next world; motion only, never the app screen

visual_language: A beat-driven monochrome teaser in which a single black dot is the protagonist: it splits, is framed, is pressed, becomes the door into a black 3D space, becomes a hole in a dot terrain, a playhead, and finally sits inside the logo. Medium: code-style flat vector plus halftone imagery placed in real 3D perspective (cards floating in depth, a dot-field terrain). Every outline is a dotted line, every image is a halftone dot screen. Typography in two sizes only: small medium-weight sans captions typed letter by letter with a round dot as the cursor, which then collapse into a Morse-like dot string, and big heavy grotesk single words in lowercase ending in a period, swapped hard on the beat in one fixed slot. Rhythm: cuts on a 0.25/0.5 s grid (consistent with about 120 BPM, not measured from the audio); eight scenes in 24 s, average about 3 s, with a burst of 0.25-0.5 s inversion cuts at 14.5-17.5 s before the payoff. Moves: fast ease-out bursts and arrivals (0.15-0.4 s), strong ease-in pushes into the dot (0.2 s), near-linear camera flights, snappy word swaps with no tween. Palette: off-white and black only, alternating between two worlds (off-white page / black space), with one-frame white or black flashes on beats; full colour is held back until the payoff card. Signature moments: push into the button that becomes the black world; dots that grow until they wipe the frame; the terrain whose ribbons go jagged with the word; the 1→2→4→8→16 inverted beat cuts; colour arriving at the end.
look: 2.5D to real 3D, unlit: flat black and off-white shapes, no shading, no shadows, no reflections, no depth of field (only perspective size and density fade with distance; far dots go grey at the horizon). Images rendered as halftone dot screens (dot size by luminance), cards as thin dotted-line rectangles on planes turned in 3D space; a ground plane of dot rows in perspective; white point specks as stars; no gradients except the haze where the dot terrain meets the horizon. Backgrounds: plain off-white page or plain black void.
code_translation: Code-native. Black space and the terrain as a three.js scene: planes with a halftone shader (dot size from image luminance, screen-space dot grid), dotted frames as instanced dots along the rectangle edge, the terrain as an instanced point grid displaced by noise and by a per-word profile, ribbons as thick line meshes, specks as points; camera flights as spline paths. The off-white page scenes as flat SVG/canvas: dot actor, dotted outlines drawn by revealing instanced dots along a path, typed captions from the shaped brand Persian font with a dot cursor at the leading edge (right to left), the Morse collapse as the text glyphs swapped for a dot string of the same width. Beat inversion cuts by swapping the background and foreground colour tokens. No lights or shadows are needed: the reference is unlit, so flat is faithful here.
continuity: One dot is the actor for the whole film: it splits, gets framed, is pressed, opens the next world and ends inside the logo.
Push into a dot: the camera pushes into a small round element until it fills the frame and becomes the background of the next scene.
Two worlds, light page and dark space, alternate; each change is a hard cut or a one-frame flash on the beat.
Dot bloom wipe: dots multiply and grow until they cover the frame, then the next world appears.
Dive through a hole: a black ellipse opens in the ground and the camera tilts down through it into the next scene.
Typed caption with a dot cursor that collapses into a Morse dot string before the next caption.
One fixed slot for big words, swapped hard on the beat; the scene below reacts to each word (shape and texture change).
Dotted outlines everywhere: frames, rings and shapes are drawn on as lines of dots, and morph between shapes on the beat.
Slots fill one by one along a dotted line while a playhead dot steps forward.
Beat-cut multiplication: each cut doubles the number of items and inverts the background.
Colour held back: the film stays black and off-white until the payoff, where real colour appears inside the hero card.
Dots converge into the final lockup; an expanding dotted ring closes the film.
risks: Third-party product teaser of unknown origin: ADAPT only. Never copy the app screen, the mood chips, the timeline UI, the wordmark or badge, the English copy, the photos and clips, the audio, or its shot order one by one.

Owner assets must not be halftoned, recoloured or cropped into dot screens (CLAUDE.md): show them unedited inside dotted frames, as the reference does with its full-colour payoff card; halftone applies only to elements we draw.

The reference is 16:9; our default is 9:16. Its left-caption / right-card layouts and the wide terrain must be recomposed for vertical (caption above, card below; terrain filling the lower half) inside the safe zone.

Captions are small (cap height about 2.5% of the 16:9 frame) and the big words swap every 0.35-0.5 s: in our film every caption meets minimum size and every word holds for the readability hold time; beat swaps are kept for single short words only.

Persian text is right to left: typing runs from the right with the dot cursor at the left edge of the text; joined letters are never split into dots; the Morse collapse replaces whole words, not letters.
The 0.25 s inversion cuts and one-frame flashes (14.5-17.5 s, 4.00 s, 21.00 s) are a flashing risk; keep them few, never above 3 flashes per second, and never under a voice line that needs reading.

The reference's two values (off-white, black) map onto the brand's light and dark neutral roles; the colour payoff maps onto the brand accent or the owner's assets; colours were read by eye, not sampled.
Audio is third-party, loud and peaks at 0 dB; it is ignored, L6 builds the sound. The 120 BPM grid is inferred from cut times only.
